title: The Water Cycle
subject: science
strengths: Most of the class can name evaporation when a puddle dries up in the sun.
The class can order the cycle stages when the sea is the starting point.

modelAnswers.question: Name the stage of the water cycle where water falls back to the ground, and say what makes it fall.
modelAnswers.answer: Precipitation: the drops in the cloud join and grow bigger and heavier until gravity pulls them down as rain.
creditPoints: Carries the working through to the correct final answer

modelAnswers.question: Put the four stages in order, starting from the sea: collection, condensation, evaporation, precipitation.
creditPoints: The sun lifts water from the sea (evaporation), it cools into a cloud (condensation), falls as rain (precipitation), then gathers in rivers and the sea again (collection), ready to start over
Carries the working through to the correct final answer

commonErrors.misconception: Water disappears for good once it evaporates.
commonErrors.example: A learner writes that the water in a dried-up puddle is gone forever and rain must be brand-new water.

fixIt.prompt: Fix it: trace where the puddle water went, stage by stage, until it falls again as rain.
fixIt.corrected: The puddle water evaporated into invisible water vapour, the vapour cooled and condensed into a cloud, and the drops fell back as precipitation - the same water, never gone.

commonErrors.misconception: Water disappears for good once it evaporates.
commonErrors.example: On the exit ticket, a learner says evaporated water disappears, so the cycle stops until new water is made.

fixIt.prompt: Fix it: explain in one sentence why evaporation does not remove water from the cycle.
fixIt.corrected: Evaporation only changes liquid water into invisible water vapour; that vapour condenses into clouds and returns as rain, so no water leaves the cycle.

nextSteps: Reteach the cycle as a loop with no water created or destroyed, tracing one drop all the way round.
Practise naming the stage at each arrow of the cycle diagram before moving on.
